1 Background

library(cellmig)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggforce)
library(patchwork)
library(skimr)
ggplot2::theme_set(new = theme_bw(base_size = 10))

2 Data (raw)

This is how a typical cell migration data looks like \(\rightarrow\) a table.

Each rows is a cell with the following features:

  • well = unique well ID (w1, w2, w3, etc.).
  • plate = unique plate ID (p1, p2, p3, etc.). A plate contains multiple wells.
  • compound = compound name (c1, c2, c3, etc.)
  • treatment dose (0, 1, 5, 10, low, mid, high, etc.)
  • v = Observed cell migration speed (numeric)
  • offset = binary (0 or 1). Indicates whether a treatment should be used for batch correction across plates. By default offset = 0 (no correction). Set to 1 for specific treatment groups (compound x dose) used as offsets. Ensure that this treatment group appears on each plate.
data("d", package = "cellmig")
d$offset <- 0
knitr::kable(d[1:10,], row.names = F, digits = 2)

In this vignette we will use simulated data from:

  • four plates: p1, p2, p3 and p4
  • 90 wells per plate: w1, w2, …, w360
  • 20 cells per well with their migration speeds v
  • the wells are treated with one of six compounds c1, c2, …, c6 at one of five doses d1, d2, …, d5. Each pair of a compound and dose is described as group: c1|d1, c2|d2, … etc.
ggplot(data = d)+
  facet_wrap(facets = ~paste0("compound=", compound), scales = "free_y", ncol = 2)+
  geom_sina(aes(x = as.factor(dose), col = plate, y = v, group = well), size = 0.5)+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        strip.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(0.03,0,0.03,0, "cm")))+
  xlab(label = "dose")+
  ylab(label = "migration speed")+
  scale_color_manual(values = c("steelblue", "orange", "forestgreen", "purple"))+
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3)))+
  guides(shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3)))

3 We can also show the mean migration per well (across all 20 cells each well)

dm <- aggregate(v~well+plate+compound+dose+group, 
                data = d, FUN = mean)
ggplot(data = dm)+
  facet_wrap(facets = ~paste0("compound=", compound), scales = "free_y", ncol = 2)+
  geom_sina(aes(x = as.factor(dose), col = plate, y = v, group = well), 
            size = 1.5, alpha = 0.7)+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        strip.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(0.03,0,0.03,0, "cm")))+
  xlab(label = "dose")+
  ylab(label = "migration speed")+
  scale_color_manual(values = c("steelblue", "orange", "forestgreen", "purple"))+
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3)))+
  guides(shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3)))

4 Model fitting

o <- cellmig(x = d,
             control = list(mcmc_warmup = 300,
                            mcmc_steps = 1000,
                            mcmc_chains = 4,
                            mcmc_cores = 4,
                            mcmc_algorithm = "NUTS",
                            adapt_delta = 0.8,
                            max_treedepth = 10))

5 What are the overall effects of compounds and doses on cell migration?

ggplot(data = o$posteriors$mu_group)+
  geom_line(aes(x = dose, y = mean, col = compound, group = compound))+
  geom_point(aes(x = dose, y = mean, col = compound))+
  geom_errorbar(aes(x = dose, y = mean, ymin = X2.5., ymax = X97.5., 
                    col = compound), width = 0.04)+
  ylab(label = "effect")

6 Compare the dose-response profiles for different compounds

get_profiles(x = o)+
  patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1, 5))

7 Compare the effects between treatment group

7.1 Pairwise dot-plot comparison \(\rightarrow\) x minus y axis

  • x/y-axis treatment groups (combinations of compounds and doses)
  • \(\rho\): Difference between treatment groups at y-x axis.
  • \(\pi\): probability of observing either a completely positive or negative \(\rho\)
u <- get_pairs(x = o)
u$plot

7.2 Violin plot based comparison

  • from_groups: vector of treatment groups to consider (combinations of compounds and doses)
  • to_group: target treatment group
  • violins show the posterior distributions of the differences (\(\rho\): each element from from_groups vs. to_group).
  • label: probability, \(\pi\), of observing completely positive or negative \(\rho\)
u <- get_violins(x = o, 
                 from_groups = c("c1|d1", "c1|d2", "c1|d3", "c1|d4", "c1|d5"), 
                 to_group = "c2|d1")
u$plot

8 Posterior predictive checks (PPCs)

g <- get_ppc_violins(x = o)
g

g <- get_ppc_means(x = o)
g

9 migcell can be used to simulate data

sim_data <- sim(N_well_cells = 30,
                N_plate = 6,
                N_group = 10,
                N_well_reps = 5,
                kappa_mu = 2,
                kappa_sigma = 0.3,
                sigma_bio = 0.3,
                sigma_tech = 0.1,
                alpha_p = rep(0, 6),
                mu_group = rep(0, 10),
                offset = 4)

sim_data$compound <- sim_data$group
sim_data$dose <- "low"

We can show the newly simulated cell migration velocity (y-axis) for each cell (dot) at plate (color)

ggplot(data = sim_data)+
  geom_sina(aes(x = paste0("group=", group), col = plate, y = v, 
                group = well), size = 0.5)+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        strip.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(0.03,0,0.03,0, "cm")))+
  xlab(label = "dose")+
  ylab(label = "migration speed")+
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3)))+
  scale_y_log10()

… or we can show the mean cell migration speed per well (dot) in each group (x-axis) and plate (color)

ggplot(data = aggregate(v~well+group+plate, data = sim_data, FUN = mean))+
  geom_sina(aes(x = paste0("group=", group), col = plate, y = v, 
                group = well), size = 0.5)+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        strip.text.x = element_text(margin = margin(0.03,0,0.03,0, "cm")))+
  xlab(label = "dose")+
  ylab(label = "migration speed")+
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3)))+
  scale_y_log10()

                              mcmc_cores = 4,
                              mcmc_algorithm = "NUTS",
                              adapt_delta = 0.8,
                              max_treedepth = 10))
